desc:
A shop is open for n minutes. During minute i, customers[i] people visit. The owner is in a bad mood during minute i when grumpy[i] = 1, and calm when grumpy[i] = 0. Visitors are satisfied only in minutes when the owner is calm.

The owner knows a trick that makes them calm for exactly minutes consecutive minutes, usable once. Choose where to use it and return the maximum number of satisfied customers over the whole day.

customers = [1, 0, 1, 2, 1, 1, 7, 5]
grumpy    = [0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1]
minutes = 3
calm anyway: 1 + 1 + 1 + 7 = 10
the trick on minutes 5..7 wins the grumpy customers 1 + 5 = 6 more
result = 16
hints: Customers in calm minutes are satisfied no matter what you do, so count them once up front.
The trick can only help in grumpy minutes. How many extra customers does it win if it covers a given block of minutes?
The extra for a block is the sum of customers[i] * grumpy[i] over it. Find the maximum such sum over all windows of length minutes.
editorial: Split the total into a fixed part, sum(customers[i] for calm i), and a gain that depends on the chosen block. The trick turns every grumpy minute in the block calm, so the gain of a block is the sum of customers[i] over its grumpy minutes.

Define lost[i] = customers[i] * grumpy[i] and slide a window of length minutes to find the largest window sum. The result is the fixed part plus that maximum. Time O(n), extra space O(1) if you compute lost[i] on the fly.
